text:
Alice: Quick design call — we need to pick a pattern for internal control-plane APIs (routing policies, quotas, rollouts UX). Options on the table: small per-team adapters, a centralized gateway, or per-node sidecars. Constraints: per-tenant quotas, routing/fallback policies, token-level telemetry, and smooth migration for existing clients. Thoughts?

Ben: Adapter-first sounds pragmatic. Keep services as they are (mix of REST and gRPC), put a thin translation layer that normalizes to protobuf, enforces auth/quotas, and emits canonical telemetry. Low risk for teams but adds more components to operate.

Carla: Gateway centralizes policy enforcement and metrics which is nice for Console UX and tracing. Easier to implement global policies (e.g., global quota limits, cross-service routing rules). Cons: can become a bottleneck and makes per-customer overrides harder unless gateway supports per-tenant config.

Devin: Sidecars give the best latency and local enforcement (ideal for Dedicated/private deployments). They make it easy to do per-node caching and local KV cache for token buckets. But they increase release surface area — updating policy logic across thousands of nodes is not trivial.

Alice: Key functional asks from Product: 1) per-route and per-tenant quotas with hard/soft limits, 2) routing policies (region -> fallback, model variant fallbacks for cost/latency), 3) rollout controls (canary %, A/B, auto-fallback), 4) accurate token accounting for billing. Also need good telemetry (token breakdown, latency by model/route).

Ben: For a gateway we could use Envoy + external rate-limit service + WASM extension for richer routing. Example sketch: ```filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.ratelimit
    config: { domain: "redwood", descriptors: [...] }
  - name: envoy.filters.http.lua
    typed_config: { inline_code: "-- translate headers, attach tenant" }
``` That lets us centralize policy while keeping hooks for custom logic.

Carla: Protobufs win for internal contracts (binary efficiency, generated clients). But we must support REST for ad-hoc tools and some partners. My suggestion: gateway exposes both REST + gRPC (httpjson->protobuf translation) so external clients can use REST while internal services talk gRPC.

Devin: Rollouts UX question: where does the Console push controls? If gateway holds policies, Console updates policy store and pushes to gateway. If sidecars enforce, Console needs a config distribution channel (config-service -> nodes). Gateway simplifies rollout visibility and immediate snapshots.

Alice: Migration plan idea: 1) Start with centralized gateway and policy store (single source of truth). 2) Provide adapters for teams that need custom translation or gradual cutover. 3) Evaluate sidecar for a small set of high-throughput services after we validate performance and op model.

Ben: Important technical detail: token accounting must be canonical. If enforcement happens in the gateway/adapters, they must run the same tokenizer as the runtime to emit `tokens_consumed` events. Otherwise billing/monitoring will diverge.

Carla: :thumbsup: on canonical tokenizer. Also we should version contracts carefully — easiest route is gateway performing content negotiation and returning deprecation warnings to clients.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary/gateway-v2 deployed to staging (sha: b3f9a).

Devin: How do we express model fallback policies? Example: if model latency > 250ms OR error_rate > 1% route to quantized-variant or fallback-region. Need a policy DSL or a small rule format that Console can edit.

Alice: Draft rule example (pseudo): `- match: {model: "*", tenant: "acme"} when: {latency_ms: ">250"} then: {route_to: "variant-quantized", percent: 100}` We can store as JSON/YAML in policy-store and expose in Console UI for rollouts.

Ben: Ops note: if gateway enforces most policies we need autoscaling plans and health shards for high-throughput customers (Dedicated). Otherwise gateway becomes single-tenant hotspot.

Carla: For per-tenant overrides, policy-store should support inheritance and override tiers: global -> region -> tenant -> route. That gives us flexibility without explosion of rules.

Alice: Action items: @Ben + @Devin spin up a short gateway POC demonstrating rate-limit + model-fallback + token accounting. @Carla prototype a tiny adapter that translates REST->gRPC + runs tokenizer to validate billing parity. We'll reconvene in 48h with results.

Devin: I'll also add a small perf test: gateway latency overhead vs sidecar baseline for embeddings and chat endpoints.

Carla: I'll sketch policy-store schema and example Console UI wireframe.

Alice: Great — thanks. If anyone objects to the gateway-first spike, speak now. Otherwise we'll proceed. :thinking:
